stem: Which compute option gives direct control of the guest operating system?

choices.B: Azure App Service

explanations.A: ACI runs containers without customer VM administration.
explanations.B: App Service manages the underlying web platform.
explanations.C: A VM exposes guest OS configuration and maintenance.
explanations.D: Functions abstracts the host OS from the developer.

stem: Which feature distinguishes containers from separate full VMs at a high level?

choices.B: Containers are finished business applications by definition
choices.D: Each container must own a separate physical server

explanations.A: Containers package applications while sharing OS kernel infrastructure.
explanations.B: Packaging does not make an app SaaS.
explanations.C: They depend on a host kernel.
explanations.D: Container hosts can run multiple containers.

stem: A short task starts when a file arrives. Which compute approach naturally matches?

choices.B: Azure Functions
choices.C: A permanently running manually managed desktop VM

explanations.A: AVD supplies desktop/app access rather than this event abstraction.
explanations.B: Events can trigger function execution.
explanations.C: That adds continuous guest management for a short event.
explanations.D: A set groups VMs rather than executing event code.

stem: What does Azure Container Instances offer?

choices.A: Managed execution of containers without managing VMs
choices.B: A finished hosted email suite
choices.D: A fleet of customer-managed desktop sessions

explanations.A: ACI abstracts the container host infrastructure.
explanations.B: That is a SaaS capability.
explanations.C: That is archive storage.
explanations.D: That is a virtual desktop scenario.

stem: What is Azure Kubernetes Service primarily suited to?

choices.B: Replacing all application data with email
choices.C: Choosing a VM's guest password only
choices.D: Serving as a storage access tier

explanations.A: AKS provides managed Kubernetes orchestration.
explanations.B: That is not container orchestration.
explanations.C: AKS manages broader container scheduling and operation.
explanations.D: AKS is compute orchestration.

stem: A container runs on a self-managed VM. Which conclusion is accurate?

choices.A: Microsoft necessarily patches every customer guest
choices.B: Containers automatically make the host SaaS
choices.D: The customer still maintains the VM guest OS

explanations.A: Host and guest duties remain distinct.
explanations.B: Container packaging does not select service model.
explanations.C: Containers still need infrastructure.
explanations.D: Packaging does not transfer host responsibility.

stem: What should guide a comparison of VMs, containers, and functions?

choices.A: Required control, packaging, event behavior, and operations
choices.B: An assumption all three have identical billing
choices.C: Only whether all three can execute code
choices.D: An assumption all three require guest OS control

explanations.A: Workload needs determine the useful abstraction.
explanations.B: Plans and meters differ.
explanations.C: That does not distinguish their operational tradeoffs.
explanations.D: Managed services abstract that control.

stem: Which statement about serverless functions is accurate?

choices.A: They use provider infrastructure while abstracting server operation
choices.B: They eliminate application error handling
choices.C: They run without any compute hardware
choices.D: They always use the same billing model

explanations.A: Servers exist even when customers do not manage them.
explanations.B: Customer logic still needs resilience.
explanations.C: Physical compute remains necessary.
explanations.D: Hosting plans differ.

stem: What is a VM Scale Set designed to manage?

choices.B: A group of VM instances with scaling capabilities
choices.D: A single storage account's archive tier

explanations.A: That is governance metadata.
explanations.B: Scale sets organize and scale instances.
explanations.C: That is identity management.
explanations.D: That is storage configuration.

stem: What does an availability set distribute VMs across?

choices.B: Every paired region automatically

explanations.A: Sets are not cross-country deployment.
explanations.B: Sets do not create multiregion replicas.
explanations.C: Those concern storage.
explanations.D: Sets reduce correlated host/rack and maintenance effects.

stem: How do availability zones differ from availability sets?

choices.B: Sets guarantee cross-region recovery
choices.D: Zones provide physically separated in-region failure boundaries

explanations.A: Zones are regional placement boundaries.
explanations.B: Sets do not provide region-wide disaster recovery.
explanations.C: Placement affects physical fault isolation.
explanations.D: Sets use fault/update domains while zones isolate facilities.

stem: One VM is deployed in one zone. What is still required to survive its zone failing?

choices.A: Other healthy instances and an appropriate failover design
choices.B: Only a resource tag saying resilient
choices.C: Only a larger disk on that same VM

explanations.A: A single zonal instance is not multizone resilience.
explanations.B: Tags do not create replicas.
explanations.C: Capacity does not provide another zone.
explanations.D: Budgets do not provide failover.

stem: A workload needs more similar VM instances as demand grows. Which option merits evaluation?

choices.B: Azure Files cloud tiering
choices.D: One availability set without additional instances

explanations.A: A lock does not scale compute.
explanations.B: That optimizes file placement rather than VM counts.
explanations.C: The service supports grouped VM scaling.
explanations.D: Placement alone does not add capacity.

stem: A VM SKU is listed in the selected region. What does that prove?

choices.B: A VM was created by the listing command
choices.C: The SKU is in the catalog, not guaranteed deployable capacity
choices.D: That the SKU is the cheapest worldwide

explanations.A: Quota is separate.
explanations.B: Read-only inspection does not allocate compute.
explanations.C: Restrictions, quota, and capacity still matter.
explanations.D: The list is not a price guarantee.

stem: What does az vm list-usage help inspect?

choices.A: Guaranteed host capacity at deployment time
choices.B: Every guest OS file
choices.C: Current regional usage and quota information

explanations.A: Quota visibility is not a capacity reservation.
explanations.B: Usage listing does not inspect file content.
explanations.C: It reports subscription usage/limits.
explanations.D: Usage does not validate logic.

stem: A selected VM size is restricted for the subscription. What is a reasonable next step?

choices.A: Ignore the restriction because the name exists
choices.B: Review approved supported sizes and quota/access constraints

explanations.A: Catalog presence does not guarantee eligibility.
explanations.B: Resolve the actual restriction within governance.
explanations.C: That does not resolve the size restriction.
explanations.D: Listing makes no reservation.

stem: Which networking component is normally required by an Azure VM?

choices.A: Network interface attached to a subnet
choices.B: Public IP in every case
choices.D: Private endpoint for the VM itself in every case

explanations.A: The VM connects through a NIC within a VNet.
explanations.B: Public IPs are optional.
explanations.C: Private circuits are not mandatory for every VM.
explanations.D: Private endpoints are service-access constructs.

stem: Which disk holds a VM's operating system?

choices.B: Only the temporary disk

explanations.A: Queues store messages.
explanations.B: Temporary storage is not the durable OS disk.
explanations.C: A set is placement metadata.
explanations.D: The guest operating system resides there.

stem: Why not store the only copy of important data on a VM temporary disk?

choices.A: Temporary disks automatically enforce business retention
choices.B: Temporary disks are always geo-replicated backups

explanations.A: Retention is not automatic.
explanations.B: They do not provide that guarantee.
explanations.C: These are different storage concepts.
explanations.D: Data can be lost through VM lifecycle events.

stem: Which component is optional for a VM with suitable private management connectivity?

choices.B: OS disk

explanations.A: The VM needs a network attachment.
explanations.B: A normal VM still needs an OS disk.
explanations.C: Compute capacity must be selected.
explanations.D: Private access can avoid internet exposure.

stem: What determines a VM's CPU and memory capacity?

choices.B: Its selected size

explanations.A: Container names do not size compute.
explanations.B: The VM size specifies compute resources.
explanations.C: Group metadata does not set size.
explanations.D: Permissions do not set CPU capacity.

stem: What can additional managed data disks provide?

choices.B: Persistent block storage for application data

explanations.A: Disks alone do not provide whole-app failover.
explanations.B: They extend durable VM storage.
explanations.C: Storage is not SaaS email.
explanations.D: Disks do not supply connectivity.

stem: Which plan correctly separates VM components?

choices.A: Image/OS disk for boot, NIC/subnet for networking, size for compute
choices.B: Resource tag for boot and budget for networking
choices.C: Public IP for all persistent storage

explanations.A: Each component serves its own role.
explanations.B: Metadata does not supply those capabilities.
explanations.C: An address is not storage.
explanations.D: Placement does not authenticate users.

stem: A team wants a managed website platform without guest OS administration. Which service fits?

choices.B: Azure Virtual Desktop

explanations.A: That transfers data physically.
explanations.B: That provides desktop/app sessions rather than this web platform.
explanations.C: It hosts web applications on a managed platform.
explanations.D: That retains guest OS maintenance.

stem: A legacy app needs unsupported OS-level components. What hosting option provides more control?

choices.B: Azure VM
choices.C: App Service assuming all OS drivers are supported

explanations.A: Functions does not provide guest kernel administration.
explanations.B: Guest OS control can meet those dependencies.
explanations.C: Managed platforms have capability boundaries.
explanations.D: Finished email does not host the custom dependency.

stem: What should be assessed before hosting an existing web app on App Service?

choices.A: An assumption code ownership transfers to Microsoft
choices.B: Only whether it already has a web address
choices.C: Supported runtime, dependencies, and configuration needs
choices.D: An assumption every executable can run unchanged

explanations.A: Customer code remains customer-owned.
explanations.B: A URL does not prove platform compatibility.
explanations.C: Compatibility matters for managed hosting.
explanations.D: Supported capabilities must be checked.

stem: How does Azure Virtual Desktop differ from App Service?

choices.A: It is the same as a web-app runtime
choices.B: It supplies virtual desktop and app experiences
choices.C: It removes the need for session-host planning
choices.D: It is a blob access tier

explanations.A: The user experience and architecture differ.
explanations.B: AVD addresses interactive desktop access.
explanations.C: Desktop capacity and configuration remain relevant.
explanations.D: AVD is not storage tiering.

stem: A containerized web app could use several Azure hosts. What must still be chosen?

choices.B: A mandatory customer-owned datacenter
choices.C: A hosting service and its operational responsibilities

explanations.A: Containers are not inherently SaaS.
explanations.B: Azure has managed container hosting.
explanations.C: Packaging alone does not select host management.
explanations.D: They can include dependencies.

stem: Which evidence strengthens a hosting recommendation?

choices.A: Only a list of resource names
choices.B: An assumption price always outweighs compatibility
choices.C: A promise that the selected service cannot fail
choices.D: Requirements mapped to platform capabilities and duties

explanations.A: Names do not demonstrate suitability.
explanations.B: A cheap incompatible platform cannot meet requirements.
explanations.C: No such general guarantee exists.
explanations.D: The rationale shows fit and remaining maintenance.

stem: Read-only SKU inspection succeeded. What Azure cleanup is required by this lab?

choices.B: None, because no resources were created

explanations.A: SKUs are provider catalog entries.
explanations.B: Catalog queries do not allocate services.
explanations.C: Unrelated resources are not part of this lab.
explanations.D: That is unnecessary and destructive.
